text_std: w?lto wteli eto ẖ?to : ẖ?k dqrite || a[pe]dem[k] tñyidmni pwrite elḫte dqrito | ẖ?ewito sno qore : lw : ewkenki : apedemki || [.][.][.][.][.][.] w [.][.][.] l : e[.][.] kkte apedemki
notes: Read sign by sign from Griffith's printed cursive type, right to left. '|' = line break in Griffith's printing (stone lines only where stated); '?' = a sign I could not settle or one Griffith himself marks '?'; [x] = Griffith's restoration in square brackets; each [.] = one of Griffith's lacuna dots (not an exact sign count). 'signs' counts read and restored signs, not [.]. Parts in order: (a) before the god || (b) before the king || (c) behind the king (end of about 15 short lines). Style d. Griffith: the first letter of (a) is 'very uncertain', perhaps a numeral; apedemk (his Apezemak) identified here; he takes sno (his 'Shane') before qore as the king's name. REM 0405 from FHN II no. 153 (Tañyidamani tablet, Baltimore WAG 22.258). FHN reads (b) ... *mewito *Mno qo*re l w ewkenki Apedemki and (a) *ato wt li eto*hto *mk dqri*te: Griffith's type has ẖ? where FHN has *m (ẖ?ewito, ẖ?k: the m/ẖ pair), s where FHN has *M (sno), and w?lto for *ato. Griffith did not read tñyidmni as a name. Check against FHN II: 83 of 89 signs agree (93.3%).
